item.title: Opening reception for Kensuke Yamada: Ceramic Sculptures — Fri Oct 30, 7:00 PM — John Natsoulas Gallery
item.description: Kensuke Yamada: Ceramic Sculptures Between Folklore and the Modern World October 28–November 28, 2026 Opening Reception: October 30, 7–9 p.m. The John Natsoulas Gallery is pleased to present a solo exhibition of ceramic sculpture by Kensuke Yamada, an artist whose distinctive figurative works fuse Japanese cultural traditions, contemporary visual culture, and an enduring fascination with the human condition. Combining references to folklore, mythology, and popular imagery with exaggerated forms and richly worked surfaces, Yamada creates figures that are simultaneously humorous, unsettling, and emotionally resonant. In this new body of work, his characteristic playfulness takes on a greater sense of urgency, reflecting the pressures and uncertainties of contemporary life. Born in Kamakura, Japan, Yamada grew up surrounded by the country’s historic architecture, religious imagery, and long tradition of ceramic sculpture. item.title: Día de Muertos: Day of the Dead Celebration — Sun Nov 1, 8:00 AM
item.description:
Celebrate Día de Muertos (Day of the Dead) in Downtown Davis! Join the community at E Street Plaza for a vibrant celebration honoring loved ones, culture, and tradition. Enjoy an afternoon and evening filled with colorful altars, live entertainment, traditional music, dancing, and family-friendly activities. Event Highlights:
12:00 PM – 7:00 PM: Altars and ofrendas honoring loved ones 4:00 PM – 7:00 PM: Welcome celebration, folklórico dance performances, mariachi music, and live band entertainment Face painting, community booths, and local vendors

item.title: Davis Odd Fellows Classic Film Fest: One, Two, Three — Sun Nov 1, 10:30 AM — Davis Odd Fellows
item.description:
Get ready for an evening of classic comedy as the Davis Odd Fellows Classic Film Fest returns with a special series celebrating the screwball comedies of the 1960s and 1970s! The series kicks off with One, Two, Three (1961), Billy Wilder’s fast-paced political comedy starring James Cagney, Horst Buchholz, and Arlene Francis. Davis Enterprise film critic Derrick Bang will introduce the film with behind-the-scenes insights and fun facts, followed by a Q&A after the screening. Enjoy live music by According to Bazooka before the movie! Admission and popcorn are FREE! Donations are welcome, and the bar will be open for beverage purchases. Doors open at 6:29 PM, and the movie begins at 7:01 PM. Everyone is welcome!
Source: Davis Downtown

item.title: Davis Odd Fellows Classic Film Fest: The Producers — Sun Nov 8, 10:30 AM — Davis Odd Fellows
item.description:
The laughs continue at the Davis Odd Fellows Classic Film Fest with a screening of Mel Brooks’ comedy classic The Producers (1968)! Starring Zero Mostel and Gene Wilder, this outrageous comedy follows a scheming theater producer and a mild-mannered accountant who hatch a plan to make a fortune from a Broadway flop. Naturally, things don’t go quite as planned! Davis Enterprise film critic Derrick Bang will share fascinating film trivia and behind-the-scenes insights before the screening, followed by a Q&A afterward. Live music by According to Bazooka will kick off the evening. Admission and popcorn are FREE! Donations are welcome, and beverages will be available for purchase at the bar. Doors open at 6:29 PM, and the movie starts at 7:01 PM. Bring a friend and enjoy a classic night at the movies!

item.description:

Directed by Peter Bogdanovich, this hilarious comedy of mistaken identities, mixed-up luggage, and unexpected romance takes audiences on a wild adventure through San Francisco. Davis Enterprise film critic Derrick Bang will introduce the movie with entertaining background details and film insights, followed by a Q&A after the screening. Enjoy live music by According to Bazooka before the film. Admission and popcorn are FREE! Donations are welcome, and the bar will be open for beverage purchases. Doors open at 6:29 PM, with the movie beginning at 7:01 PM. Don’t miss the final screening of this classic comedy series!

item.description: On an annual basis, the Davis Cemetery District hosts a Dia de los Muertos (Day of the Dead) celebration on our grounds. This celebration is one of the last Mesoamerican indigenous influenced rituals, honoring mother earth and all ancestors. This celebration is part of an effort to create a community, a sense of belonging, and global awareness of cultural richness in our multicultural society. The Davis Cemetery District’s annual Día de los Muertos public altar was set up on Thursday, October 29th and will remain in place through November 2nd. In addition to the public ofrenda, we will offer grave cleaning supplies, and educational signage highlighting the traditions and significance of Día de los Muertos. This year will also feature a designated pathway decorated with marigolds and papel picado, encouraging visitors to stroll through the cemetery, reflect, and honor the memories of their loved ones. item.title: Light & Grain — Fri Oct 30 — The Artery
item.description:
The Artery presents “Light & Grain,” a two-person exhibition featuring oil painter Kristina Kernytska and woodworker Viktor Ivantsov. The exhibition runs October 30 through November 23, with an artists’ reception on Friday, November 13, from 6–9 p.m., coinciding with the Davis Second Friday ArtAbout. “Light & Grain” brings together two distinct approaches to natural beauty: the raw, carved grain of wood and the vibrant, textured light of oil paint. Kristina Kernytska’s paintings and Viktor Ivantsov’s wood carvings invite viewers to experience nature through texture, memory, and light. Together, the works celebrate the landscapes and living world that inspire both artists.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Manetti Shrem Museum: Together Again, 1960–2026, Perspectives from UC Davis’ Fine Arts Collection — Fri Oct 30, 10:00 AM — Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis
item.description: Together Again inaugurates the Manetti Shrem Museum’s ongoing collection galleries. This exhibition highlighting the collection will be on long-term view, accompanied by temporary exhibitions each fall and winter. The ongoing collection galleries trace a history of art forged from UC Davis and throughout Northern California. By focusing on relationships of many kinds, this presentation proposes that in order to understand an artwork in all its fullness, chance encounters and long-standing friendships often matter as much as formal affiliations. UC Davis legends such as Wayne Thiebaud, Deborah Butterfield and Bruce Nauman are exhibited alongside important regional voices that were once overlooked, and the exhibition extends to the artists shaping Northern California today, including Sadie Barnette, Woody De Othello and Ruby Neri. Together Again builds bridges between who we were and who we are becoming at UC Davis, and affirms the Manetti Shrem Museum as home to the complex story of No

item.title: Out of Line: Art at the Edge — Fri Oct 30, 10:00 AM — Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis
item.description:
Inspired by conceptual artist Bruce Nauman’s video work “Dance or Exercise on the Perimeter of a Square (Square Dance), 1967–68,” this exhibition explores Davis as a site of both artistic practice and political protest. Mike Henderson, Ester Hernandez, Malaquías Montoya, Bruce Nauman, Nancy Rubins, Dorothy Wiley and the student artists of UC Davis’ Third World Forum engage with film, print and performance to confront who they were and what their work meant in a world of radical change. They made work wherever and however they could: in collaborative workshops, student newsrooms, kitchens and living rooms. While rooted in the politics of the late 20th century, “Out of Line” finds renewed meaning in the present day.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Birds & Bikes — Fri Oct 30, 12:00 PM — Axis Gallery
item.description: Axis Gallery is proud to announce Birds & Bikes, a collaborative art exhibition bringing together regional artists to explore the poetic intersections of avian flight and human motion. Running from October 2 through November 1, 2026, the exhibition showcases a dynamic range of works from intricate metal sculptures and imaginative textile art to curated gallery shop goods, celebrating the beauty of migration alongside the engineering of daily travel. The exhibition features a direct partnership with the City of Sacramento Office of Arts and Culture (OAC) Art in Public Places program and North Natomas Jibe. Birds & Bikes serves as an artistic tie-in to the upcoming Birds and Benches project, which will install artist-designed public benches across North Natomas Regional Park. Visitors are invited to experience the unique ecology and transit identity of the Natomas Basin through a collaborative lens, discover one-of-a-kind art pieces, and browse handcrafted items in the East Gallery Pop

item.title: Weekly Game Night at Blue Note — Wed Jan 13, 5:00 PM
item.description:
Yolo County Board Game Gathering Update 8/14/25: **We're still active**, but we primarily use Discord to chat and plan events. (See group description for invite link.)
We still meet every Wednesday for board games at Blue Note Brewing Company. We'll have a handful of tables reserved near the back; just look for the pile of board games.
People usually start arriving around 5pm, and games start whenever people are ready. Blue Note closes at 9pm, and although we have a 5-10 minute grace period there, you should be in the process of final scoring by 9, or else pack it up and play again another day.
Game night is open to all ages! Blue Note is a brewery, not a bar, so there's no restriction against minors. In addition to their crafted-in-house beer selection, water and sodas are available.
You're not required to buy anything in order to join us, but we do encourage you to support local businesses. Blue Note's chef team makes a mean pizza, and there are other nearby downtown restaurants
